entries.summary: Anselm von Rosenberg ( Rosenberg ) erhängt sich. Bischof Gottfried Schenk von Limpurg nimmt aufgrund der Freiheit Kaiser Friedrichs III. dessen Güter und das ihm verpfändete Amt Prosselsheim ( Brassoldshaim ) in Besitz. Fries verweist außerdem auf einen Bericht über den Fund der Leiche sowie einen Vertrag zwischen Bischof Rudolf von Scherenberg und Anselm von Rosenbergs Tochter.

entries.english: Anselm von Rosenberg, Ritter, hanged himself during the rule of Gotfried von Limpurg, Bischof, on the Saturday before the Annunciation of Mary in 1454. Therefore the bishop, by virtue of the aforesaid privilege, took possession of Anselm’s goods and the Amt Prosselsheim that had been pledged to him by the bishopric. Evidence was taken about how he hanged himself and was found, in the fourth register of Rudolf’s contracts, fol. 191. [Several earlier readings and a reference to a 1461 date are crossed out.] Editorial note: The dispute over the properties continued for decades and was decided only by a privilege of Emperor Friedrich III in 1486, which explains the anachronistic wording.

facts.content: had his goods and Amt Brassoldshaim seized by Gotfried von Limpurg after his death; the Amt had been pledged to him by the bishopric.
